subject: Discovery Recap: MedSecure - Private/VPC requirements
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@medsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery Recap: MedSecure - Private/VPC requirements

Hi Laura — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we’re aligned on scope, pain, and next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points and goals
- Regulated PHI workflows: you need an inference stack that never leaves your VPC and meets strict audit requirements.
- Key management: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for all persisted artifacts and backups.
- Network constraints: egress restrictions, strict IP allowlists, and limited outbound connectivity in certain environments (possible air-gapped segments).
- Cost predictability: predictable throughput for batch inference during nightly processing and low-latency for customer-facing features.

Current stack and constraints (what you said)
- Primary infra: AWS GovCloud for production workloads; some dev/test still in standard us-east-1.
- Model runtimes: internal fine-tuned models (PyTorch/ONNX) with a custom KV-cache layer and tokenization pipeline.
- Security posture: existing HSM for signing, centralized SIEM, and strict change control.

Success criteria for a pilot
1) Deployment into your VPC with no egress of inference data outside your account.
2) KMS/HSM integrated for key lifecycle management and audit trails.
3) Demonstrated latency SLO (p95 < 350ms for interactive calls) and nightly batch throughput of X tokens/min with reserved capacity.
4) SOC2-ready audit evidence and logging forwarded to your SIEM.

Technical risks we flagged
- Air-gapped segments may require offline install artifacts and manual infra prep.
- KMS/HSM integration complexity differs by provider and may add ~2-3 weeks to onboarding if an on-prem HSM is used.

Next steps (agreed)
1) Redwood: share this recap + self-host install checklist and high-level network diagram (attachment: medsecure_private_vpc_recap.pdf). Action: Dylan — by EOD 8/22.
2) MedSecure: confirm list of IP ranges and egress policies; provide SOC2 report and the contact for your security review. Action: Laura — by 8/25.
3) Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60–90 min session with your infra/security team to walk through KMS/HSM options and network setup. Proposed window: week of 8/31.
4) Procurement intro: loop in procurement for early contract/PO discussion and any required SLAs.

Attachments: medsecure_private_vpc_recap.pdf (high-level checklist + network questions)

Thanks — happy to adjust if anything is missing.

— Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
D: (415) 555-0112 | dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@medsecure.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medsecure.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: MedSecure - Private/VPC requirements

Dylan — thanks for the clear recap, this matches our notes. A few clarifications and asks: 

- Confirmed: production must run in our AWS GovCloud account and not cross into public Redwood-hosted endpoints.
- We will provide the IP ranges and egress policy doc by 8/25 as requested.
- Security: attaching the SOC2 request checklist we use (see medsecure_soc2_request.pdf). Can you confirm what evidence Redwood can provide for logging/audit and if you support pushing logs to our Splunk instance or if we need to pull?
- For KMS: our preference is to use our on-prem HSM for key generation and keep private keys within our HSM. Is that supported, or would Redwood need a connector?

Procurement is looped in here to start the contractual conversation — procurement@medsecure.com will follow up on PO and standard NDA/DPAs.

Let’s plan the technical deep-dive for the week of 8/31. I’ll propose times after I sync internally.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director of Infrastructure | MedSecure
laura.bennett@medsecure.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: MedSecure - Private/VPC requirements

Looping in infra and onboarding owners — quick checklist for prep before the 8/31 deep-dive:
- Prepare an architecture sketch for GovCloud deployment (VPC setup, subnets, NAT/egress patterns, SG/ACL requirements).
- KMS/HSM options: document our supported connectors (AWS KMS, external HSM via PKCS#11/connector patterns) and what requires an on-site agent.
- Logging integrations: steps to forward audit logs to Splunk (token-based forwarder or syslog endpoint) and retention behavior.
- Offline install path: package dependencies and signed install artifacts for air-gapped install.

I’ll start a shared Drive folder (link posted to related_links) and we should draft a short playbook for the pilot runbook + runbook items needed from MedSecure (contacts, accounts, firewall change window).

— Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@medsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: MedSecure - Private/VPC requirements

Thanks Laura — great. We’ll: 
- Confirm the KMS/HSM connector matrix and send the short evidence list for SOC2 by tomorrow EOD.
- Add Splunk-forwarding steps to the runbook and include the network/IPs you can expect to see from our side.
- Marcus to share the GovCloud architecture sketch before the deep-dive.

Next meeting: will wait for Laura’s proposed times for week of 8/31 and reserve 60–90 minutes.

Talk soon.

— Dylan
